solutions.check: bars rebuilt from the blog's numbered answers (unique); every answer written into it with each crossing agreeing

clue.text: Wee stain spelling area of wet mud

blocks.note: sp. is the dictionary abbreviation for spelling
a latch is a Scots and dialect word for a mire or boggy patch

explanation.surface: A small stain spells out a muddy patch, like a Rorschach blot read as a puddle.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Wee' is the Scots word for small, flagging that the answer is Scots too: a splatch is a Scottish splotch.
explanation.definitionFit: Splatch is a Scots word for a blot or splash of dirt, so a small stain fits.

clue.text: This fortune-teller calls art? Is crystal ball possibly

indicators.note: possibly says the letters could be arranged otherwise, so they are reshuffled
the answer together with these extra words makes up the fodder, so they must be taken away again

blocks.note: the full fodder, taken as written
the letters to set aside once the fodder is rearranged

explanation.surface: A clairvoyant gazes at her crystal ball, and someone wonders whether it counts as art.
explanation.walkthrough: A composite anagram: the answer plus CALLS ART has the same letters as IS CRYSTAL BALL, so rearrange and remove CALLS ART.
explanation.definitionFit: A sibyl was a prophetess of the ancient world, and Sybil is the stock name for a seer or fortune-teller.

clue.text: Family of lice like this to catch in gym are on the rise

indicators.note: in places the preceding words inside the word for a school exercise class
in a down clue, rising means the letters read upwards, from bottom to top

blocks.note: so means in this way
to cop is to catch or nab
PT, physical training, is school gym
taken as written

explanation.surface: A naturalist describes catching lice in the school gym, where they are multiplying.
explanation.walkthrough: PT, physical training, is the British school name for gym classes. 'Like this to catch' reads as one phrase but is two pieces.
explanation.definitionFit: Psocoptera is the insect order of booklice and barklice, a taxonomic grouping of louse-like insects.

clue.text: Faithful about family king abandoned, marking direct descent

indicators.note: abandoned says the royal letter is left out of the family word
about means the word for faithful goes round what follows

blocks.note: leal is Scots for loyal or faithful
kin are your family
K is the chess abbreviation for king

explanation.surface: A loyal family history notes where the king walked out, a break in the royal line.
explanation.walkthrough: Leal is an old Scots word for loyal, as in 'the land o' the leal'.
explanation.definitionFit: Lineal descent goes in a direct line from parent to child, so lineal describes that unbroken ancestry.

clue.text: Covenant reached by doctor, character closing surgery

indicators.note: the character closing a word is its final letter, the one that ends it

blocks.note: to doctor a patient is to treat them
the final letter of surgery

explanation.surface: An agreement is struck by a doctor at the end of surgery hours.
explanation.definitionFit: A treaty is a formal agreement between parties, which is what a covenant is.

clue.text: Product of hydrolysis requiring instruments and electromotive force

blocks.note: cellos are stringed instruments
E is the physics symbol for electromotive force

explanation.surface: A chemistry lab notes a reaction that apparently needs instruments and an electric push.
explanation.definitionFit: Cellose, or cellobiose, is a sugar formed when cellulose is broken down by hydrolysis.

clue.text: They're familiar to printers old and new in newspaper section

indicators.note: in places the preceding pair of letters inside the newspaper's initials

blocks.note: the FT is the Financial Times
O is a standard abbreviation for old
N is a standard abbreviation for new
s. abbreviates section

explanation.surface: Printers, past and present, know their way around a section of the newspaper.
explanation.walkthrough: O and N go inside FT, then S for section follows.
explanation.definitionFit: Fonts are sets of type in one design and size, the everyday stock of a printer's trade.

clue.text: Imagine once e.g. breaking hand in two places

indicators.note: breaking says the abbreviation splits the other word open and sits inside it
two places means the break happens twice, so the inserted letters are separated from each other

blocks.note: fin is slang for a hand
taken as written

explanation.surface: Imagining, say, a broken hand with two fractures.
explanation.walkthrough: 'In two places' means the break happens twice: E goes after the F and G after the I, so the two letters are not kept together.
explanation.definitionFit: Feign once meant to invent or imagine, an obsolete sense, hence 'once' in the definition.

clue.text: Regular course test including a short piece?

indicators.note: including means the test word holds the next piece inside it

blocks.note: an oral is a spoken examination
a bit is a small piece

explanation.surface: A course assessment that includes a short piece of writing.
explanation.definitionFit: An orbital is the circuit a body travels repeatedly round another, a path followed regularly.

clue.text: Instrument essential to tune bells

indicators.note: essential to means the word lies at the core of the words that follow

blocks.note: the letters run across the gap between the two words

explanation.surface: An instrument needed to tune a set of bells.
explanation.definitionFit: The nebel is an ancient Hebrew stringed instrument, probably a kind of harp or lyre.

clue.text: Furrowed part of the US bordering another

indicators.note: bordering means the first part surrounds the second on both sides

blocks.note: the US is divided into states
RI is Rhode Island, another US state

explanation.surface: A tourist describes a ploughed region of America next to its neighbour.
explanation.walkthrough: RI is the postal abbreviation for Rhode Island. The blog doubted the adjective use, but the print Chambers and the OED both give striate as an adjective.
explanation.definitionFit: Striate means marked with fine parallel grooves or lines, so furrowed fits.

clue.text: Godless hiding gun in disguised terrine

indicators.note: something disguised has its appearance altered, so the letters are rearranged
hiding means the scrambled dish conceals the next word inside it

blocks.note: taken as written
to gun an engine is to rev it

explanation.surface: A heathen smuggles a firearm inside a disguised pâté.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Gun' looks like a weapon but is the verb, as when a driver guns the engine.
explanation.definitionFit: Irreverent means lacking respect for sacred things, close to godless or impious.

clue.text: Ally constant in axis, say

indicators.note: in puts the constant inside the word that follows

blocks.note: the axis is the second vertebra of the neck, a bone; say marks it as an example
c is the symbol for a constant, such as the speed of light

explanation.surface: A wartime partner who stood firm within the Axis powers.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Ally' and 'axis' paint wartime alliances, but an ally (or alley) is a playing marble, and the axis is a neck vertebra.
explanation.definitionFit: A bonce is a large playing marble, and an ally is a choice marble, so the two are interchangeable.

clue.text: Speak incomprehensibly, horse refusing jump?

blocks.note: first meaning: to gibber or jabber
second meaning: a horse that jibs, balking at a fence

explanation.surface: A rider babbles nonsense as the horse refuses a fence.
explanation.definitionFit: Jibber is a variant of gibber, to babble, and also names a horse given to jibbing, stopping short.

clue.text: Cable maybe chaps fitted in east when missing – here's proof

indicators.note: missing says the following word is left out of the compass direction
fitted in means placed inside what follows

blocks.note: taken as written
as can mean when, as in 'as the sun rose'
Vince Cable is a former British Liberal Democrat leader; maybe marks him as one example
chaps are men

explanation.surface: Installers lay a cable in the east, and a missing man's whereabouts become the evidence.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Cable' reads as a wire but is a politician, Vince Cable, former UK Business Secretary.
explanation.definitionFit: Evincement is the act of showing clearly or proving, so something that evinces is proof.

clue.text: I cackle wildly – it'll stop mount skidding

indicators.note: wildly means the letters are thrown about in no set order

blocks.note: taken as written

explanation.surface: Someone cackles wildly at the thing that keeps a horse from slipping.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Mount' is a horse, not a hill.
explanation.definitionFit: An ice-calk is a spike on a horseshoe that grips icy ground, so it keeps the horse from sliding.

clue.text: Relaxed no longer, when in grip of destiny

indicators.note: in the grip of means held inside the word that follows

blocks.note: your lot is your fate or destiny
as can mean when

explanation.surface: Someone can no longer relax once fate has them in its grip.
explanation.walkthrough: 'No longer' marks an obsolete form: loast is an old past participle of loose.
explanation.definitionFit: Loast is an obsolete form meaning loosed, so it means relaxed or set loose in old writing.

clue.text: Small constellation, one with twinkly tail

indicators.note: something twinkly flickers and shifts, so the letters move about

blocks.note: an means one
taken as written

explanation.surface: A little star group with one twinkling star trailing behind it, like a comet.
explanation.definitionFit: Antlia, the Air Pump, is a small faint constellation of the southern sky.

clue.text: Australian shrubs cover one fresh pulled up

definitions.note: plural, while the answer is singular; the name covers the genus

indicators.note: in a down clue, pulled up means the letters are read from the bottom upwards

blocks.note: a hat covers the head
a means one
raw means new or fresh

explanation.surface: A gardener covers one newly uprooted plant from the outback.
explanation.definitionFit: The waratah is an Australian shrub with large red flower heads, the floral emblem of New South Wales.

clue.text: Fruit tasted, ready for plucking?

blocks.note: a plum is a fruit
ate means tasted or consumed

explanation.surface: Fruit sampled and judged ripe enough to pick.
explanation.walkthrough: The surface reads 'plucking' as picking fruit; the definition means plucking a bird, so feathered.
explanation.definitionFit: Plumate means feathered or plume-like, and only a feathered bird can be plucked.

clue.text: Is it squidged in pats round either edge of river?

definitions.text: Is it squidged in pats round either edge of river?

indicators.note: squidged means squashed out of shape, so the letters are rearranged
either edge points to the letter at the start or end, which here are the same
round means the scrambled letters go around the single letter

blocks.note: taken as written
river begins and ends with the same letter

explanation.surface: Wondering whether that is something squashed into pats on a riverbank.
explanation.walkthrough: The whole clue is both wordplay and definition: otter droppings are left in small heaps beside rivers.
explanation.definitionFit: Spraint is otter dung, deposited in pats along the edges of the rivers otters live in.

clue.text: Paler or trembling, like lips?

indicators.note: trembling suggests shaking about, so the letters are disturbed

blocks.note: taken as written

explanation.surface: Asking whether lips turn paler or start trembling, as with fear or cold.
explanation.definitionFit: Preoral means situated in front of the mouth, which is where lips are; the question mark admits the stretch.

clue.text: Wherein to find elite RA working?

definitions.text: Wherein to find elite RA working?

indicators.note: working means set in motion, so the letters are put to a new use and order

blocks.note: RA is a Royal Academician, taken as written

explanation.surface: Asking where you would find a top Royal Academician at work.
explanation.walkthrough: The whole clue is the definition as well as the wordplay; an RA is a member of the Royal Academy of Arts in London.
explanation.definitionFit: An atelier is an artist's studio or workshop, exactly where an Academician would be at work.

clue.text: First sign of racism in school creating turmoil as before

indicators.note: the first sign of a word is its opening letter
in places that letter inside the name of the school

blocks.note: Stowe is an English public school in Buckinghamshire
the opening letter of racism

explanation.surface: A racist remark at a boarding school causes uproar, just like last time.
explanation.walkthrough: 'As before' marks an old word; the blog's commenters thought it redundant, as Chambers does not mark stowre obsolete.
explanation.definitionFit: Stowre is a variant of stour, an old word for tumult, commotion or conflict.

clue.text: Unploughed field due to knowledge number's left in places

indicators.note: left means departed, and in places says it goes from more than one spot

blocks.note: learning is acquired knowledge
n stands for an unspecified number in maths

explanation.surface: A field stays unploughed because of what a farmer knows about the numbers.
explanation.walkthrough: Both Ns go from LEARNING. A lea-rig is a Scots term.
explanation.definitionFit: A learig is a grassy ridge left unploughed in a field, from lea, meaning untilled grassland.

clue.text: What's next to do? Think about filling in that CV

indicators.note: about means turned around, so the thinking word runs backwards
filling in means stuffed inside the preceding letters

blocks.note: in the sol-fa scale do is followed by re
to muse is to think

explanation.surface: A jobseeker wondering what to do next is told to think about completing a CV.
explanation.walkthrough: 'What's next to do?' sounds like a career question but means the note after do in do-re-mi.
explanation.definitionFit: A résumé is the American term for a curriculum vitae, a summary of your career.

clue.text: Plant bodies Aegean island's reared

indicators.note: reared means raised up, so in a down clue the letters read upwards

blocks.note: Samos is a Greek island in the eastern Aegean

explanation.surface: Plants grown on a Greek island.
explanation.definitionFit: Soma is the biological term for the body of an organism apart from its reproductive cells, plants included.

clue.text: Wildcat grabbing swan's tail in savage struggle

indicators.note: a word's tail is its final letter
the struggle word grabs and holds the letter within it

blocks.note: a maul is a violent scrum or brawl
the last letter of swan

explanation.surface: A wild cat seizes a swan by the tail in a vicious fight.
explanation.definitionFit: The manul, or Pallas's cat, is a small wild cat of the Central Asian steppes.

clue.text: Wood? River circles small one

indicators.note: circles means goes all the way round what follows

blocks.note: the Tees is a river in north-east England
a small, abbreviated river is R

explanation.surface: A river winds round a little wood.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Small one' refers back to river: R is its abbreviation. The question mark marks wood as an example of trees en masse.
explanation.definitionFit: A wood is a collection of trees growing together, so the trees make up the wood.

clue.text: Wine holds up, short time bottled

indicators.note: up in a down clue means the word reads from bottom to top
bottled means held inside, as in a bottle

blocks.note: to have is to hold
yr is the short form of year

explanation.surface: A wine that keeps well, bottled after only a short time.
explanation.definitionFit: Syrah, also called Shiraz, is a red grape variety and the wine made from it.

clue.text: Neutering precludes this cross-breed – nothing smelly

blocks.note: a zo is a cross between a yak and a cow
O is zero
gamy, or gamey, means strong-smelling like high game

explanation.surface: A vet notes that neutering stops a pungent hybrid animal from breeding.
explanation.definitionFit: Zoogamy is sexual reproduction in animals, which neutering makes impossible.

clue.text: Tall Pacific tree, piece incorporated in cross

indicators.note: incorporated in means taken inside the following word

blocks.note: a tau cross is T-shaped, named after the Greek letter
a man is a piece in chess or draughts

explanation.surface: A section of a tall island tree built into a crucifix.
explanation.definitionFit: The tamanu is a large tree of the Pacific islands and South-East Asia, valued for timber and oil.

clue.text: Snare-maker maybe creating fury, restrained by women's resistance

indicators.note: restrained by means held in check between the letters that follow

blocks.note: W is an abbreviation for women
ire is anger or fury
R is the symbol for electrical resistance

explanation.surface: A trapper's anger is kept in check by women resisting him.
explanation.definitionFit: A wirer is someone who sets wire snares for game, so a snare-maker is one example.

clue.text: Rite suffused with an aura, as the case determines? (10, three words)

indicators.note: suffused means spread through and mixed, so all the letters are blended together

blocks.note: taken as written
taken as written

explanation.surface: A ceremony steeped in a mystical glow.
explanation.definitionFit: A natura rei is Latin for from the nature of the thing, so it means as the matter itself determines.

clue.text: Part of golf club: selected club lost latitude

indicators.note: lost means the word for selected has dropped the card-suit letter

blocks.note: chose means selected
C stands for clubs, the card suit
L is an abbreviation for latitude

explanation.surface: A golfer's chosen club has lost its range.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Club' repeats the definition's golf club but here means the card suit.
explanation.definitionFit: The hosel is the socket of a golf club head into which the shaft fits.

clue.text: Tangle in one end of leash at full stretch

indicators.note: in one means in a tangle itself, so the word is knotted into a new order
end points to the final letter of the following word

blocks.note: taken as written, and also the image of the scrambling
the last letter of leash

explanation.surface: A dog walker gets tangled in the leash as the dog pulls as far as it can.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Tangle in one' means put the word tangle into a tangle, so the fodder doubles as its own instruction.
explanation.definitionFit: A-length is an old adverb meaning stretched out at full length.
